acknowledgement: My sole research target is the full quadratic-form statement: for arbitrary independent real coordinates with densities bounded by one and arbitrary real symmetric A with at least three eigenvalues of absolute value at least one, prove one universal density bound for X^T A X or give a valid counterexample.

first_essential_unresolved_implication: Remove the equal-eigenvalue/rank-one structure in the codimension-one same-sign branch, then bridge from only three arbitrary large eigendirections without selecting a dimension-losing fixed coordinate minor.
